scope: job platform only: real PostgreSQL + RabbitMQ, synthetic handler, no model/IMAP/SMTP/OSS calls
workerModel: all workers of one configuration share a single Node process
caveats: Workers for a configuration run inside one Node process, so CPU-bound configurations under-report multi-core scaling; the production topology is one worker per pod, scaled horizontally.

The handler is synthetic: no model, IMAP, SMTP or OSS calls are made. These numbers measure the job platform (PostgreSQL + RabbitMQ round-trips and lease bookkeeping), not end-to-end business latency.

The single-mailbox configuration is serialized by design (head-of-line ordering prevents a reschedule being applied before the original invitation), so its lower throughput is a correctness property rather than a regression.
Percentiles come from per-job rows in PostgreSQL (queue wait, end-to-end) plus in-process handler timings (service time), so they can be recomputed from raw.jsonl.

metricsOverhead.conclusion: delta is within the observed run-to-run spread
metricsOverhead.note: Paired interleaved runs compared by median; the spread across identical runs is reported so a noisy machine cannot be presented as instrumentation overhead.

serializationBound.note: One mailbox is processed strictly in order, so this is the designed per-mailbox bound, not a regression.

poolSizing.note: Worker count, not SQL, sets the pool requirement: claims, heartbeats and outbox publishes each borrow a connection.

failurePath.note: Terminal failures are recorded once and never retried, so a permanently broken mailbox cannot cause a retry storm.
